title: Fermat's little theorem over the axiom-free naturals: a^p is congruent to a modulo any prime p
statement: For every natural number p that is prime -- primality spelled inline as the conjunction of 2 <= p and (for all d, d divides p implies d = 1 or d = p), there being no `Prime` name in this kernel -- and every natural a, a^p is congruent to a modulo p. Congruence is Nat.modEq, defined here as `modEq d a b := exists u v, a + d*u = b + d*v`, an existential over natural witnesses rather than a statement about a remainder operation. The carrier renders as `AxNat`; despite the name it is an INDUCTIVE type, not an assumed one, and the `nat` prelude's trusted surface measures 0 (axiom=0, opaque=0, quotient=0). The proof is constructive throughout: no excluded middle, no propext, no funext, no Quot.sound. This is the unrestricted form a^p = a, NOT the coprime form a^(p-1) = 1, which is not established here and needs cancellation by a modulo p (see notes).

formal.statement: ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : And (AxNat.le (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) x0) (((x2 : AxNat) -> ((x3 : AxNat.dvd x2 x0) -> Or (Eq.{1} AxNat x2 (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) (Eq.{1} AxNat x2 x0))))) -> AxNat.modEq x0 (AxNat.pow x1 x0) x1)))

evidence.supports: `Nat.pow_prime_modeq_self` is admitted by the kernel with exactly the type in formal.statement, and `Nat.add_pow_modeq_prime` -- the Frobenius identity (a+b)^p = a^p + b^p mod p that Fermat's induction rests on -- is admitted alongside it. Both are pinned by the same test, so the identity Fermat depends on cannot drift while Fermat's own statement stays fixed.

evidence.notes: A footprint check cannot carry this claim: a theorem stating something weaker -- primality replaced by 0 < p, or the vacuous a = a -- has exactly the same empty footprint. Mutation-verified rather than assumed: transposing the exponent in the pinned string (AxNat.pow x1 x0 -> AxNat.pow x0 x1) makes cargo report `43 passed; 1 failed`, naming this test and no other; restored, 44/44 green. The test re-derives from source on every run, rebuilding the whole Nat prelude through add_declaration. Anchored on the exact `1 passed; 0 failed` count, so an unmatched filter -- which prints `running 0 tests ... ok` and exits 0 -- cannot read as success.

Nat.euclid_lemma was admitted and axiom-free but named by NOTHING in this prelude's sweep until 2026-08-23, so it was never visited -- axiom_footprint of an unvisited name is not empty, it is unmeasured, and the two are indistinguishable in a green run. It is registered now, and Fermat depends on it transitively. The pinned count in the_build_is_deterministic is a live guard: changing 20+142 to 20+143 killed exactly one test when checked.

prior_art.what: the congruence a^p = a (mod p) for p prime
prior_art.where: letter to Frenicle de Bessy, 18 October 1640; stated without proof
prior_art.attribution: standard attribution. Fermat stated it and did not publish a proof; the first published proof is Euler's (1736). This lane consulted no primary source.

prior_art.what: an unpublished proof by the multinomial/Frobenius route
prior_art.where: unpublished manuscript, cited in the standard histories
prior_art.attribution: conventional; noted because the route proved here -- via (a+b)^p = a^p + b^p mod p -- is the one attributed to Leibniz and later Euler, not Fermat's own.

notes:
WHICH FORM THIS IS. The unrestricted a^p = a (mod p), true for every a including multiples of p. The coprime form a^(p-1) = 1 (mod p) is NOT established here and does not follow without cancellation by a modulo p -- a Nat analogue of Int.modEq_cancel, itself an Euclid's-lemma development. The lane flagged that as a blocker rather than starting one in the last stretch of a slice. Recorded so the two forms are not conflated.

THE ROUTE WAS CHOSEN BY MEASUREMENT, NOT PREFERENCE. A lane sent at Fermat earlier the same day scouted both classical proofs and reported the permutation argument -- x |-> a*x permutes the nonzero residues mod p -- UNREACHABLE in this kernel: there is no Finset, no bijection, and no injective-on-a-type notion, which is a subsystem rather than a lemma. That report is why no effort went into the dead route, and why the binomial route's single missing piece (Nat.prime_dvd_choose) was identified and dispatched instead.

The Frobenius identity Nat.add_pow_modeq_prime is a result in its own right and is pinned by the same test. It is where primality actually enters: every interior binomial coefficient C(p,k) with 0 < k < p is divisible by p, so the whole interior of the expansion vanishes modulo p and only the two end terms survive.

external_status is `proved`: this is formalization of a known theorem, not discovery.
